```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
knitr::knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) x <- format(x, big.mark = ",")
  paste(x, collapse = ", ")
})
```

A MetaMorpheus export has two peptide sequence columns: `Full Sequence`,
which includes the modifications, and `Base Sequence`, which does not. MSstats
needs the sequence with the modifications, since otherwise the modified and
unmodified forms of a peptide are merged into one feature. In the rows that a
language model is shown, the two columns are often the same, since most
peptides carry no modification. This vignette shows the two columns, the
example rows where they look the same, and what the choice does to the
differential abundance analysis. The conversion specification and the results
of the analysis were obtained once and saved, so the vignette runs without a
language model or the full export.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(MSstatsConvertLLM)
library(data.table)
```

# The export

We use the MetaMorpheus output of the Solivais2024 benchmark, in which
*E. coli* proteins are spiked in different amounts into a constant human
background. We distribute the rows of the export that the model was shown. The
benchmark of the manuscript normalized the column names before showing them to
the model, replacing spaces and other characters by dots, and the conversion
specification uses these names. In these rows, the base and the full sequence
are the same.

```{r export}
case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "metamorpheus_case_study.rds",
                            package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
export <- normalize_headers(case$rows)
export[, .(Base.Sequence, Full.Sequence, Precursor.Charge, Peak.intensity)]
all(export$Base.Sequence == export$Full.Sequence)
```

# Inferring the conversion specification

`infer_specification()` sends the model the column names and the first
`r formals(infer_specification)$n_preview` rows of the export. We obtained the
saved conversion specification with the call below, using llama3.1-8b and the
lean prompt, in the benchmark of the manuscript.

```{r infer-live, eval = FALSE}
specification <- infer_specification(export, "llama3.1-8b", "lean",
                                     acquisition = "DDA")
```

Here, we read the saved conversion specification instead.

```{r infer-saved}
specification <- case$specification
as.data.frame(specification$mappings)[, c("field", "from", "confidence")]
```

# Checking the peptide sequence

The model chose `Base.Sequence`, the sequence without the modifications. The
example rows give no reason to prefer either column, since the two are the
same there. They differ on modified peptides. The export reports the peptide
below with and without the oxidation of a methionine, in the same run, at the
same charge and in the same protein group.

```{r forms}
forms <- normalize_headers(case$forms)
forms[, .(Base.Sequence, Full.Sequence, Precursor.Charge, Peak.intensity)]
```

Read by the full sequence, the two rows are two peptides. Read by the base
sequence, they are one, and the LLM-based converter takes them as two
measurements of one feature and keeps the larger.

```{r count-forms}
c(full = uniqueN(forms$Full.Sequence), base = uniqueN(forms$Base.Sequence))
```

The hand-written converter, `MetamorpheusToMSstatsFormat()`, reads
`Full Sequence`, which `GROUND_TRUTH` lists for the peptide sequence.

```{r gold-standard}
GROUND_TRUTH$metamorpheus$PeptideSequence
```

# Differential abundance results

We converted the full export with the hand-written converter, which reads
`Full Sequence`, and with the LLM-based converter and the model's conversion
specification, which reads `Base Sequence`. We then analyzed both with
MSstats, as below. The script `compare_solivais.R` in the GitHub repository of
the package runs these steps, after keeping the peaks of single human or
*E. coli* protein groups.

```{r analysis-live, eval = FALSE}
peaks <- fread("QuantifiedPeaks.tsv")
annotation <- fread("annotation.csv")

converted <- list(
  hand = MSstatsConvert::MetamorpheusToMSstatsFormat(peaks,
                                                     annotation = annotation),
  llm  = LLMtoMSstatsFormat(normalize_headers(peaks), annotation = annotation,
                            llm_mapping = specification))
processed <- lapply(converted, MSstats::dataProcess,
                    normalization = "equalizeMedians")
# contrast: each condition against condition A
compared <- lapply(processed, function(p) MSstats::groupComparison(contrast, p))
```

Here, we read the saved results instead. They have one row per protein and
comparison. For each converter, they give the adjusted p-value, `adjp_h` for
the hand-written converter and `adjp_l` for the LLM-based converter, and
whether the protein was called significant, `sig_h` and `sig_l`. `spiked`
marks the *E. coli* proteins, whose amount changes in every comparison, and
`in_h` and `in_l` say whether each converter's results include the protein. A
protein that MSstats could not test, because one condition has no measurement,
is never called significant, whatever its adjusted p-value.

```{r results}
results <- case$results
head(results, 3)
```

For each comparison, the table below counts the proteins called significant
with each sequence column, and the *E. coli* proteins among them.

```{r counts}
counts <- results[, .(full        = sum(sig_h, na.rm = TRUE),
                      full_spiked = sum(sig_h & spiked, na.rm = TRUE),
                      base        = sum(sig_l, na.rm = TRUE),
                      base_spiked = sum(sig_l & spiked, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(comparison = Label)]
counts
```

A call changed when one converter called the protein significant and the
other did not. We count it as near the threshold when the converter that did
not call the protein significant still gave it an adjusted p-value of `NEAR`
or less.

```{r changed}
NEAR <- 0.2
changed <- results[in_h & in_l][xor(sig_h %in% TRUE, sig_l %in% TRUE)]
near <- changed[pmax(adjp_h, adjp_l, na.rm = TRUE) <= NEAR]
c(changed = nrow(changed), near_threshold = nrow(near))
```

Over the `r nrow(counts)` comparisons, the base sequence changes the call of
`r nrow(changed)` proteins, `r nrow(near)` of them near the threshold.

# What to check

- Which column the conversion specification reads as `PeptideSequence`. It
  should be the sequence with the modifications, `Full Sequence` in
  MetaMorpheus.
- Do not judge the two columns by the example rows alone, where they are often
  the same. Look for the rows where they differ, for example with
  `export[Base.Sequence != Full.Sequence]` on the full export.
- A peptide that the export reports with and without a modification must stay
  two features.
